state.seed_assertion: Intermittent faults are most commonly hardware-related or caused by installation problems, while software problems are typically less intermittent than they appear.

sentences.1: Intermittent faults are most commonly hardware-related or caused by installation problems, while software problems are typically less intermittent than they appear.
sentences.2: From my experience, intermittent faults are most commonly hardware related either damaged product or a problem with the installation.
sentences.3: Software or firmware are root cause in some cases.
sentences.4: In reality most software problems are not as intermittent as they may seem.
sentences.5: If the system has been in production for a long time and suddenly intermittent faults start to appear, the first question to ask yourself is what changed, software? Hardware? The manufacturing process?
sentences.6: Temperature-related failures may appear only after warm-up or washdown.
sentences.7: Temperature-related failures may appear only after warm-up or washdown.
sentences.8: Software faults tend to be repeatable and occur when a specific set of conditions is present, whereas hardware faults are affected by environmental conditions.
sentences.9: Aliasing can occur when high-frequency, high-power signals from power supplies and drivers appear in other systems or at different time scales.
sentences.10: Aliasing, often a hardware issue, can be another difficult item to examine.
sentences.11: These appear randomly, making systematic testing difficult.
sentences.12: Different fault types in PLC systems show distinct patterns that indicate whether the problem is hardware failure, software bug, or configuration error.
